AfterCardPlayed.maps_to: on_card_played (tuning_fork.py:29-36), dispatched by HookSystem.on_card_played (hooks.py:385-389) from CombatState._resolve_card_play (combat.py:514)
AfterCardPlayed.issue: Rollup of guard G1 per binding rule 4. Every clause of the relic is faithful -- the Skill test, the >= threshold, the `-= threshold` rather than a zeroing, the 10 and the 7, and (contrary to its own docstring) the per-run counter -- but the sim fires this hook ONCE PER PLAY where C# fires it once per REPLAY ITERATION, so a replayed Skill advances the counter by 1 instead of 2.

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): a replayed Skill counts once instead of twice, so the counter drifts and every later trigger in the run is one Skill late
guards.issue: MECHANISM (residual after the in-loop move): the per-Replay-iteration half of this gap IS closed -- sts2_rl/combat.py:589-591 computes `play_count` once, :610 loops it, and :638-639 dispatches `self.hooks.on_card_played(card, is_auto_play)` INSIDE the loop, matching CardModel.cs:1904/1959. Executed: with `_skills_played` preloaded to 9 and a Defend played under relic/throwing_axe the sim now prints counter 1 / block 17 (the game's value; was 0), and a Defend with `base_replay_count = 1` advances the counter by 2. What remains is the GUARD on that dispatch. combat.py:638 gates the call on `if not self.is_over_or_ending:` (combat.py:922-944 = COMBAT_OVER or player dead or all enemies dead), and the comment at combat.py:633-637 asserts "The C# test is `IsOverOrEnding`". THAT COMMENT IS FALSE (PROMPT.md bug class 24): CardModel.cs:1957 tests only `CombatManager.Instance.IsInProgress`, and Hook.cs:272-286 dispatches `Hook.AfterCardPlayed` through `combatState.IterateHookListeners()` DIRECTLY -- deliberately bypassing `IterateCombatHookListeners`' IsOverOrEnding bail (Hook.cs:53-63), with the source's own summary saying "Dispatched directly, not through the IterateCombatHookListeners guard: it completes resolution of the card that caused the kill." Teardown is deferred to CheckWinCondition, so IsInProgress is still true at :1957. NET EFFECT: a Skill whose play lands the killing blow counts in the game and does NOT count in the sim, so `SkillsPlayed` (a [SavedProperty], run-scoped -- see N1) is left one Skill LOW for the rest of the run, the same never-washing-out drift this guard was opened for, only in the opposite direction. With a replay source it is worse: combat.py:640-641 also breaks the play-count loop on `_all_enemies_dead()`, where CardModel.cs:1960-1963 returns early only on `Owner.Creature.IsDead`, so a Throwing-Axe-doubled Skill that kills on iteration 0 counts TWICE in the game and ZERO times in the sim. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed today, ported content only): tuning_fork alone, counter 0, enemy at 1 HP, a Strike seeded on top of the draw pile, `cards/havoc.py` (a CardType.SKILL whose on_play auto-plays that Strike) played from hand -- the enemy dies and `_skills_played` ends at 0 where TuningFork.cs:99-101 gives 1. Both sides ported: Tuning Fork is Uncommon in the transcribed grab bag, Havoc is a registered Ironclad Skill, Throwing Axe is granted by the ported Tanx shrine (events/tanx.py:13). Single-arm: `grep -n is_parity sts2_rl/combat.py` returns nothing, so the legacy RL leg and the parity leg share the defective gate. This is the seam's `Hook.AfterCardPlayed` dispatch guard (audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json) surfacing at Tuning Fork's own observable; the seam owns the machinery, this record owns the counter. Rule 7: combat.py, hooks.py, cards/havoc.py, events/tanx.py, relics/throwing_axe.py, src/Core/Hooks/Hook.cs, src/Core/Combat/CombatManager.cs and audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json are NOT hashed by this record. guards.what: N3: the order of GainBlock and the decrement -- C# grants the block and THEN does `SkillsPlayed -= SkillsThreshold` (TuningFork.cs:105-106); the sim decrements first (tuning_fork.py:34-36)
guards.rationale: Nothing reads SkillsPlayed between the two statements except DisplayAmount (TuningFork.cs:25-35), which is presentation, and CreatureCmd.GainBlock cannot re-enter AfterCardPlayed. So the two orders reach the same state. Recorded because it is exactly the kind of ordering that would matter if the block gain ever triggered another Skill play -- the sim's order is the safer one, and it is not a divergence today.

guards.what: N4: `SkillsPlayed >= SkillsThreshold` and `-=` rather than `== threshold` and `= 0` (TuningFork.cs:102, 106)
guards.rationale: tuning_fork.py:33-34 uses the same `>=` and the same subtraction. This is load-bearing precisely BECAUSE of G1: in the game a replay can push the counter to 11 in one play, and `>=` plus `-= 10` leaves 1 rather than swallowing the overflow. The port would therefore behave correctly if G1 were fixed, without a second change -- worth stating so the fixer does not touch this arithmetic.
